title: The Wars of the Roses
objective: After this level you can explain the fight between two families for England's crown.
summary: From 1455 to 1485 the houses of Lancaster and York fought for England's throne. Henry Tudor won at Bosworth, where Richard III died; Richard's skeleton turned up under a Leicester car park in 2012.

cards.headline: In 2012, archaeologists dug up a car park in Leicester and found a king.
cards.body: He had died in battle in 1485, at the end of a thirty-year family feud over England’s crown. How did that feud start, and how did it end?

cards.headline: Two houses, one crown
cards.body: From 1455 to 1485, two branches of one royal family, the houses of Lancaster and York, fought for the throne. Both were descended from Edward III. The trouble began at the top: King Henry VI suffered spells of madness, and powerful nobles with private armies ran riot. The first battle came at St Albans in 1455. A family inheritance fight, with armies instead of lawyers.

cards.headline: Roses, added later
cards.body: Nobody at the time called them the Wars of the Roses. The name came long afterward, from the supposed badges of the two sides: the white rose of York and the red rose of Lancaster. A lovely name for a very bloody business.

cards.headline: Bosworth, and a wedding
cards.body: On 22 August 1485 Henry Tudor defeated Richard III at Bosworth Field, and Richard was killed. As Henry VII, he married Elizabeth of York in 1486, joining the rival claims in one marriage and founding the Tudor dynasty. The feud that started with a battle ended with a wedding.

cards.headline: The king in the car park
cards.body: Richard’s grave was lost for centuries. In 2012 a University of Leicester team dug where the Grey Friars church once stood, now a car park, and found a skeleton with a curved spine and battle wounds. DNA matched living relatives of his family line, and in 2013 the university announced it was Richard III beyond reasonable doubt.

questions.prompt: The Wars of the Roses were fought between the houses of _____.

options.label: Tudor and Stuart
options.rationale: The Tudors came out of the wars.

options.label: Plantagenet and Norman
options.rationale: The rivals were Lancaster and York.

questions.explanation: The houses of Lancaster and York, both descended from Edward III, fought from 1455 to 1485.

questions.prompt: Put these events of the Wars of the Roses and after in order, from earliest to latest.
items: The first battle came at St Albans
questions.explanation: The first battle came at St Albans in 1455. Henry Tudor defeated Richard III at Bosworth in 1485 and married Elizabeth of York in 1486. In 2012 a Leicester team found Richard’s skeleton.

questions.prompt: The Sutton Hoo ship grave held no body at all. What confirmed that the Leicester car-park skeleton was Richard III?

options.label: A gravestone bearing his name
options.rationale: His grave was lost for centuries.

options.label: DNA from his family’s living relatives
Chemical traces left in the acidic soil
options.rationale: That was Sutton Hoo’s missing body.
